snippet.title: Firefly Lane Behind the Scenes
snippet.description:
Going behind the scenes of Netflix’s Firefly Lane is a wild ride! The TV series follows two best friends, Kate and Tully, played by Sarah Chalke and Katherine Heigl over the span of many years. After doing a major deep dive, I learned that the show actually follows the book super closely! Even with things like action and dialogue. There were also some fun facts shared by Ben Lawson about the scene where Johnny and Kate accidentally take ecstasy. They got the actors some dilated pupil contacts to really sell their high, and Ben randomly put on one of Kate’s leg warmers just because he thought it would be appropriate for someone who was high. This was also Katherine Heigl’s first time shooting a nude scene ever in her career! She was sold on it by the director Anne Wheeler because of her artistic vision for it, but she was super nervous getting it shot, especially at this point in her career. The only thing she requested was that she sees the scene when it was finished, but ultimately, she felt safe shooting it with Anne. Katherine Heigl and Sarah Chalke also played their nineteen-year-old characters and they ended up having to use a bit of CGI to get it done. At first, they were using face tape, but apparently, they just looked like they had bad facelifts, so they opted for the CGI softening route. We’ve got a lot of Firefly Lane to unpack here, so stick around!

So, we all love Puss in Boots from both the Shrek movies and from his own movies and TV series, right? At least, we hope you do! Cause this adorable and feisty hero is a classic animated character. And of course, behind these characters are all the incredible actors who voiced them. In this video, we’re taking a look behind the scenes at the famous names who have lent their voices to the characters in this awesome movie. Of course, it features big names like Antonio Banderas and Salma Hakey Pinault, but it also brought in the insane talents of people like Harvey Guillen, Florence Pugh, John Mulaney, and Wagner Moura. We’ll give you some inside scoops on what each of them thought of the process of voicing these amazing characters, and how it made them feel to be a part of the movie. You’ll see clips of them in the studio recording their characters’ voices, as well as interviews where they give their thoughts about the movie, the process, and their characters. It’s a great glimpse into the world of voice acting, of Puss In Boots, and of movie making in general! snippet.title: Twilight Reboot: What We Want to See
snippet.description:
We have exciting news for you, whether you’re Team Edward or Team Jacob! Lionsgate TV is looking to turn the Twilight franchise into a new TV series, and in celebration of that news, we’re going over everything that we want to see in this reboot! For example, we thought that the original cast, composed of stars such as Kristen Stewart, Robert Pattinson, and Taylor Lautner, did a great job in the Twilight movies, and so we would like to see them receive cameo appearances in this new series! That being said, we have already come to accept that we’ll be getting a mostly original cast for this project, and we’re hoping that we might be getting a more diverse cast, sort of like what director Catherine Hardwicke pictured when she was casting for the first movie. Stephanie Meyer didn’t like the idea of her deviating from the original descriptions of the characters from the Twilight books, which is the reason why we didn’t get to see it the first time around, but we’re hoping to see something a little different this time! Beyond that, we are also hoping to see some slightly better special effects than what we got with the horrifying CGI monstrosity that was Renesmee in Twilight: Breaking Dawn Part 2! This doll was so terrifying that it even earned a nickname that was inspired by Chucky from Child’s Play, which really doesn’t bode well for the prop’s screen presence! Still, we can’t wait to revisit the Cullen family soon!

snippet.title: Why Pedro Pascal HATES The Mandalorian Beskar Armor
snippet.description:
It’s definitely not an easy task to be Pedro Pascal on the set of the Disney Plus show, The Mandalorian. As you know, the show is a spin off of the star wars series, so naturally, it’s going to have some insane costumes. Although we absolutely love Pedro Pascal as Mando, he actually really hates the costume! After doing a bit of research, it’s not super surprising. First of all, he’s pretty much blind with that helmet on. The only thing he has to look through is a narrow slit that’s often fogged up by his own breath. It’s also super heavy! The thing is extremely weighted down and the costume designers have gone over it more than once in an attempt to make it a bit more comfortable for him, but alas, they were never quite successful. Luckily, he does have two body doubles to take the pain away from him from time to time, but of course, Pedro Pascal does all the voice lines for Mando. Which, speaking of, fans often ask him to do the voice outside of work without the helmet on and it’s probably the most cringe thing you can think of. He describes it as this low register bedroom voice and without the mask it’s really, really awkward. He’s done the voice a few times for young kids at the request of their parents and he said it must be really awkward for whoevers walking by because he’s just whispering to a six-year-old. There’s a lot to unpack here!

I also can’t wait to get my hands on the blooper reel for this film because you know it’s gonna be fire – the vibes on this set are so good, you can tell they are all lifelong friends at this point. snippet.title: Harry Potter Reimagined as a Disney Movie
snippet.description:
Have you ever wondered what your favorite Harry Potter characters would look like if they were reimagined in the world of the Walt Disney Company? In celebration of the recent announcement that HBO Max would be rebooting the Harry Potter franchise, we’re trying to imagine what it would look like if Disney got their chance to animate the Wizarding World as well! Daniel Radcliffe did a great job being the face for the Boy Who Lived across multiple movies, but for our animated movie, we imagine that he would look something like Prince Eric from the Little Mermaid. We’re casting a character that looks something like Moana for Hermione, even though we loved Emma Watson in the role as well! When it comes to Ron, Rupert Grint simply lacked the towering height that J.K. Rowling described him as having in the books, and so for his animated character, we would like to see something like Kristoff from Frozen! We also get a glimpse into what Ron and Hermione might have looked like if they’d gotten to dance with one another at the Yule Ball in a picture that’s inspired by Beauty and the Beast. Evanna Lynch called out the design for our Disney-fied version of Luna Lovegood herself, praising a picture that seemed to have the same big eyes as Anna and Elsa from Frozen. Albus Dumbledore bears a striking resemblance to Merlin from the Disney animated movie The Sword in the Stone, and although we loved Michael Gambon and Richard Harris in the role, we’d be excited to see who Disney would cast!

snippet.title: What We Want to See in the New Harry Potter Series
snippet.description:
What are you most excited to see done in the HBO Max Harry Potter TV series? This reboot is going to give us an entirely new take on some beloved characters, most of which we haven’t gotten to see since the last Harry Potter movie! Daniel Radcliffe took on the role of Harry Potter originally, and while we can’t imagine a better actor for the Boy Who Lived, we’re hoping to see someone with passion and a new take on the character approach it on the HBO series. Emma Watson played Hermione Granger in the movies, and she’s gone on to have quite the prolific acting career since then, appearing in things like the live action remake to Beauty and the Beast from the Walt Disney Company. Rupert Grint took on the role of Ron Weasley, and although we loved him for it, we’re still hoping to see a slightly more book-accurate version of the character make it to the screen this time around. Ron isn’t the only Weasley we’re hoping to see a more book-accurate version of in this remake either; Ginny, played by Bonnie Wright in the movies, could also use a major update this time around! The movies also featured such incredible talent as Alan Rickman, Maggie Smith, and Michael Gambon, and so it’s going to be very difficult for the HBO series to find a cast to rival the original one! snippet.title: Celebrities Who Look Shockingly Similar
snippet.description:
It’s shocking how many celebrities are walking around with similar looks and real-life doppelgangers. It’s definitely a theme that I’ve discovered that they all typically tend to enjoy playing into the gag and even going as far as taking credit for one another’s work or signing autographs. Lucy Hale gets mistaken for Selena Gomez so often that one time in an airport an older woman came up to her and approached her as a huge fan and when she found out the woman thought she was Selena, she didn’t have the heart to tell her that she was in fact, not Selena Gomez, but Lucy Hale. Sarah Hyland and Mila Kunis also love being mistaken for one another because, one, Sarah Hyland has always been a huge fan of Mila Kunis, and two, Mila loves it because Sarah is much younger than her so she always takes it as a compliment. There’s also Halsey and Millie Bobby Brown. Back in 2016, Halsey was Millie Bobby Brown’s character, Eleven, from Stranger Things for Halloween and has stated more than once that the resemblance is uncanny. She wants to do a biopic and she would love to cast Millie as her – they have often been told that they could truly be sisters. Sigourney Weaver and Susan Sarandon are always getting mistaken for one another, with Susan taking credit for “Alien” on more than one occasion and Sigourney signing autographs for Susan. It’s clear that people who pretend to be others for a living have no problem doing it in real life as well!

snippet.title: Severus Snape & Other Characters Based on Real People
snippet.description:
Some movies are biopics that go out of their way to tell you that they’re entirely based on real events; these aren’t those movies. Instead, these are the fictional characters who drew influence off of real life people that you might not have known about. Plenty of the characters from the Harry Potter franchise are based off of people that J.K. Rowling knew in her personal life, from her childhood friends to the teacher who taught her chemistry! The Marvel Cinematic Universe provides us with a few examples on this list as well; for example, Tony Stark drew so much influence from the real-life figure of Elon Musk, that it even led to him receiving a cameo in Iron Man 2! Meanwhile, J. Jonah Jameson of the Spiderman movies including Spider-Man: Far From Home is actually based on someone who may surprise you, considering very few of us can imagine Stan Lee so angry. From the Star Wars film franchise, we learn that Jabba the Hutt is actually based on one actor from Casablanca. Harley Quinn of the DC Extended Universe was actually inspired by the very first actress to have ever portrayed her. And did you know that Sylvester Stallone actually faced a lawsuit from boxer Chuck Wepner over the Rocky film franchise? The Walt Disney Company provides us with two characters who were based off of real life people, the first one being Ursula from the Little Mermaid, who was actually based on the drag performer Divine, and the last one being Christopher Robin from Winnie the Pooh.

snippet.title: What Wednesday Would Look Like in a Disney Movie
snippet.description:
Have you ever imagined what the Netflix series Wednesday would look like if it had been made as an animated movie by the Walt Disney Company instead? We’re picturing some of our favorite characters as they would behave and appear in such a movie, and taking inspiration from other movies from Disney and Pixar in order to do it! As a Disney princess, Wednesday Addams really reminds us a lot of Belle from Beauty and the Beast. She’d have to swap out the iconic presence of Jenna Ortega for big eyes and straight-across bangs of Cinderella though, albeit with her hair done up black instead of blonde! Tyler Galpin, who is portrayed by Hunter Doohan on the Netflix show, would actually have a surprising amount of similarities to Hans from the Disney animated feature Frozen. We imagine that the character brought to life by Christina Ricci, Laurel Gates, would probably have a design that is quite similar to Bellwether from Zootopia, if you only imagined her more as a human than as an anthropomorphized sheep! As a siren, Joy Sunday’s Bianca Barclay automatically strikes up some comparisons to Ariel from the Little Mermaid, or even the sea monsters from Luca, which really makes us think that Disney would probably try to give us a meeting between two different worlds with this type of movie! Bianca’s rivalry with Wednesday would most likely remind us of the dynamic between Vidia and Tinkerbell from Disney’s animated fairies franchise. Meanwhile, Percy Hynes White’s Xavier would most likely feature a design that would have some similarities to Camilo from Encanto.

snippet.title: Harry Potter Actors Who Were Recast
snippet.description:
The making of the Harry Potter movies was chaotic to say the least! Many actors had to be replaced over the course of years worth of filming, and for multiple reasons too. Richard Harris passed away, which forced the director of Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban, Alfonso Cuarón, to seek out another actor for the role of Dumbledore. He eventually found the perfect actor in Michael Gambon, although the role has also been taken on by Jude Law in the Fantastic Beasts series, and it is set to be recast again in the wake of the news of the upcoming HBO Max series. Warner Bros. decided not to replace the actor of Vincent Crabbe, even after Jamie Waylett had lost the role, and so his character was just sort of replaced with Blaise Zibini. The actress who first appeared as Pansy Parkinson has actually gone on to a surprisingly successful acting career; you can see Genevieve Gaunt on the E! original series The Royals. The original actor to take on the role of Bill Weasley was eventually replaced by Domnhall Gleeson, the son of Brendan Gleeson, the actor of Mad-Eye Moody. And did you know that Robert Pattinson wasn’t the first actor to appear as Cedric Diggory? At the end of the day, we’re just glad that Warner Bros. never needed to replace any of our main cast members! The Harry Potter movies simply would not feel the same if it didn’t have Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson, Rupert Grint, or Tom Felton in the roles they were given!

snippet.title: Avatar and Other Movies That Completely Copied Better Ones
snippet.description:
Sometimes, it really does seem as though Hollywood has run out of ideas! These ten movies completely ripped off better ones, some of them copying mere premises, while others went so far as to take their titles and cover art too! We’ll be talking about James Cameron’s Avatar, and how it has come under fire for its similarities to movies like Dances With Wolves, Pocahontas by the Walt Disney Company, and the 20th Century Fox animated film FernGully: The Last Rainforest. The Force Awakens ripped off A New Hope, even though both of them are entries into the Star Wars franchise. But as George Lucas pointed out, every new entry into the franchise should explore a new world or landscape, which The Force Awakens did not. Ratatoing is only one of many examples of a low-budget knock off to an animated classic! You may also be familiar with Chop Kick Panda, copying Kung Fu Panda of DreamWorks Animation, and Tappy Toes which ripped off Happy Feet from Warner Bros. Pictures. The Fast and the Furious screenwriter admitted to ripping off a little-known Keanu Reeves movie from the 1990’s known as Point Break, also starring Patrick Swayze and Lori Petty. Mac and Me is basically the exact same movie as Steven Spielberg’s E.T., but with one massive difference: Mac and Me was actually funded in part by McDonald’s, and even included Ronald McDonald in a scene! The Hunger Games became a massive success, starring Jennifer Lawrence, Liam Hemsworth, and Josh Hutcherson, but many have pointed out that it bears a few striking similarities to a certain Battle Royale.

snippet.title: Tetris: Behind the Scenes
snippet.description:
Let’s go deep behind the scenes of Apple’s new movie, Tetris! Starring Taron Egerton as Henk Rogers, this movie is based on true events and is an absolute whirlwind! There is a ton of accuracy behind the film – one thing for sure is how many laws Henk Rogers broke in the Soviet Union. Everyone in his life advised him not to go over there, but he risked his life for Tetris! The story has a lot of touching elements – one of the main themes is actually friendship! Henk Rogers’ friendship with Alexey Pajitnov is one of the driving forces behind the massive success that is Tetris. Henk was the first person Alexey could ever talk with about computers. He describes Tetris as his little baby and he never thought in a million years that he would actually get to make money from it – he was just so passionate about tech and computers at the time. There were also a ton of delays due to Covid which had an effect on the film. For one, they weren’t able to shoot in Moscow, so they had to opt for Scotland, which ended up working out better for everyone at the end of the day. If it hadn’t been in Scotland and during Covid, they would have never been able to shoot that car chase at the end of the movie! In the first few drafts it wasn’t even in there, but they wanted to amp up the stakes in a creative way so they took liberty with a car chase. There’s a lot to unpack, so stick around!

snippet.title: Dream Casting: Our Top Picks for a Harry Potter Reboot
snippet.description:
Have you heard the good news? HBO Max seems to have their eye on adapting J.K. Rowling’s Harry Potter books into an entire series, adapting one book every season. This would mean that we would have to update the cast away from the one we knew from the movies, including Daniel Radcliffe and Emma Watson, and although it’s hard for us to imagine anyone doing a better job than them, a new cast doesn’t necessarily have to be a bad thing! We explore fifteen options for a new cast. None of these are being officially considered (so far as we know), it’s all just for fun and the love of the Harry Potter franchise! We suggested Adam Driver for the role of Severus Snape, seeing as he’s already played a somewhat similar role as Kylo Ren on the Star Wars franchise. Mark Addy has worked with HBO before, seeing as he played King Robert Baratheon on Game of Thrones, and we can see him making a perfect Vernon Dursley! We suggested Karen Gillan, from the Guardians of the Galaxy movies of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, for the role of Lily Potter, and fellow Avengers alumni Aaron Taylor-Johnson for the role of James Potter. Multiple actors who have appeared in Peter Jackson’s Lord of the Rings universe made it onto this list as well, including Andy Serkis who played Gollum, and Martin Freeman and Benedict Cumberbatch from the Hobbit trilogy. Michael Caine was a brilliant mentor to Batman in the Dark Knight franchise, which is part of the reason we think he’d be great as Dumbledore!

snippet.title: Bad Movies With Great Premises
snippet.description:
Have you ever watched a movie that has a killer premise, only to discover that they somehow managed to make a subpar product? It’s definitely a frustrating experience, especially when you know that there was so much potential there. It’s almost worse than when a movie is just bad from start to finish, and you know all the reasons why. But when the premise is solid, it feels like the whole thing is a bigger letdown. In this video, we’re taking a look at some of the movies that suffered from this particular affliction. Movies that had so much coolness to go off of, and yet they somehow didn’t quite turn out. Now, it doesn’t mean they weren’t successful. One of them, for example, ended up being the 4th highest grossing movie of that year. Another one did so well at the box office that it spawned a sequel. But even those movies were considered huge disappointments by critics and audience members, because they could have been amazing, yet weren’t. We’ll talk about movies with really cool concepts, like using time as currency, or being able to teleport whenever you want. We’ll talk about movies based on super successful books, so you know that the material and the premise were already there. And yet the movie versions turned out less than great. And what’s wild is that most of them had A-list, bankable stars in them. So that theoretically should have helped some. But often, it didn’t. So check out this video today, as we explore some bad movies that had great premises!

snippet.title: 8 Times Actors Went Too Far On Set
snippet.description:
Whoever said acting was a fun job?! I don’t know about you, but after seeing everything that Heath Ledger went through to play his characters in Joker and Brokeback Mountain, I have a whole new respect for these hard working actors. The fact that it took Leonardo DiCaprio four decades and the experience of eating raw bison and sleeping inside an animal carcass to earn an Oscar is very telling! There are so many actors who take their method acting way too far on set and do some really insane things! Ashton Kutcher landed himself in the hospital not once, but twice, for his performance of Steve Jobs in the 2013 biographical film “Jobs.” Even his wife, Mila Kunis, said he was taking it way too far! There are also the questionable actions of Jamie Dornan when he was trying to get into the mind of his character on “The Fall.” He actually full-on stalks a woman he saw randomly at the train station! He said he felt incredibly dirty doing it, but he learned some valuable stuff when it came to playing his character. Rooney Mara also went through some intense body modifications for her role in “The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo.” For her it was really important to get those things done because it was like a second costume due to how much nudity there was in the movie. snippet.title: Why Jenna Ortega is the Best Wednesday Addams

Okay, obviously we are all here because we love Jenna Ortega’s portray as Wednesday Addams on the hit Netflix TV series, “Wednesday.” If that’s not why you’re here, I’m definitely going to convince you otherwise. There have been other incredible performances of the iconic character – one being Christina Ricci, of course, who also stars alongside Jenna, and the incredible Lisa Loring. I’m not here to say anything negative at all about these other two actors – I’m just here to say that I think Jenna Ortega was the best choice for Wednesday’s teen years. Tim Burton and the entire production team also agree! One thing you might not know about Jenna is that she’s been compared to the character of Wednesday her entire life. She’s always had this very dry sense of humor and she easily incorporated that into her character. She also worked incredibly hard to bring her to life – she constantly walked like Wednesday while the cameras weren’t rolling, she learned cello, fencing, and German, just for the show. It’s clear that she’s a perfectionist and she puts all of herself into her work. It even started showing in her wardrobe! Her closet somehow seemed to lose all of its’ color after she started as Wednesday. There’s a lot to unpack about Jenna Ortega’s performance and if I can’t convince you she was the best choice, I really don’t know what could! snippet.title: Actors Who Were ALMOST Cast in Harry Potter
snippet.description:
The Harry Potter franchise has jump-started the career of many well-known actors, but did you know that the franchise could’ve been completely different? Obviously, Alan Rickman was absolutely iconic as Snape and we couldn’t imagine Hagrid being anybody else, but what if? We almost had actors like Robin Williams, Ian McKellen, and Eddie Redmayne as major roles in the Harry Potter world. There were a lot of reasons why these actors weren’t cast in the first place, from having a British-only rule to being too young, too old, or too funny, but it didn’t stop them from trying! Ian McKellen was offered the role of Dumbledore, which wasn’t too much of a stretch considering he played Gandalf in The Lord of the Rings franchise, but Ian didn’t feel comfortable taking the role because he knew his predecessor wouldn’t approve. Robin Williams really wanted the role of either Hagrid or Lupin, but because he wasn’t British, they couldn’t cast him. Kate Winslet was considered for Rowena Ravenclaw, but rumor has it her agent didn’t think the role was prominent enough for her career. There was also Hugh Grant, who got his career started in 1997 from Four Weddings and a Funeral. He very well could have shown up in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets as Gilderoy Lockhart, but because of scheduling conflicts, he had to turn down the role. There are so many actors who could’ve been cast that it raises the question of what the films would’ve been like if they’d gone through with it!

snippet.title: Yellowjackets: Things You Missed
snippet.description:
Did you notice how many easter eggs and hints were dropped throughout Showtime’s Yellowjackets? I had to go behind the scenes to find out everything I could about any upcoming plot points or things you could miss with just one watch-through. With major names like Christina Ricci and Elijah Wood on the show, you know it’s gonna be stellar. Something pretty interesting as a recurring theme of the show is the mysterious friendship necklace. It seems to make its way through the group of girls, always ending up on one who meets a tragic end. There are also some major hints dropped with the music that was meticulously thought and planned out by the music supervisors. I also have some big theories about who our Antler Queen could be, mostly due to one perfectly timed shot that seems to be giving a major clue. There was also an astounding amount of foreshadowing about what happens to Jackie, even some eerie lines said by both her and Taissa. It’s like the writers were telling us exactly what would happen to her right under our noses. There’s also a lot to say about the visions that these girls keep having – one in particular being Lottie. Do you think she really saw what would happen to Laura Lee when she got on that plane? A lot of fans think she did. Every secret Yellowjackets is trying to keep is going to be unpacked in this video, so make sure you stick around to catch it all.

snippet.title: Shazam Movies Without VFX
snippet.description:
If you’re a fan of the Shazam! movies, then you know how visually amazing they are. The VFX teams who worked on them are definitely wizards at their craft, and it paid off. There are mind blowing sequences throughout the movies that feature all kind of flying, morphing into different characters, mid-air fights, and realistic looking monsters with smoke hovering around them. But of course, none of that would look realistic if it wasn’t for the brilliant VFX work they did. In this video, we’re taking a look at some great Shazam footage without the VFX, so you can see exactly what it’s like filming a movie like this. Plus it’s really cool to see what the before and after shots look like, so you get a glimpse behind the curtain for what making heavy VFX movies is really like. We take a look at their use of what are known as ‘tuning fork rigs,’ showing actors like Zachary Levi and Mark Strong pretend to fly as they are manipulated on these gyroscope-like devices. We show some of the wire rigging that ultimately got painted out by the VFX team, which not only includes actors, but also an 1800 pound bus that was dangling off of a bridge.  And we take a look at some scenes where you can see what was originally there before it was replaced by incredible looking monsters. It’s a fun mix of CGI, practical effects, and more. So check out this video today if you’re a fan of the Shazam! movies, so you can see what they look like without VFX!
